guide.summary: OpenProject documents OAuth2 authorization code flow where the app acts on behalf of the current user via a bearer token. Each customer instance needs an OAuth application registered by an administrator with a redirect URL and client credentials. The api_v3 scope is the standard API scope and is the only documented scope needed for the work package list endpoint, which supports offset pagination. Read the subject property for titles. The connected person's existing access to work packages is a user prerequisite, not an extra OAuth scope. Setup and execution remain untested.

findings.title: Authorization code flow acts on behalf of the connected user
findings.detail: OpenProject's OAuth2 server offers an authorization code flow; the resulting bearer token lets the app make API calls on behalf of the current user. Client credentials is also documented but is not needed for connected-person access.
findings.appliesWhen: Connected customer person authorizes the app.

findings.title: Each customer instance administrator must register the OAuth application
findings.detail: Administration > Authentication > OAuth applications is where the application is created on each OpenProject instance. The administrator must note the Client ID and secret and configure a redirect URL. Only administrators can create OAuth apps.
findings.appliesWhen: Every customer instance connects with its own registration.

findings.title: api_v3 scope for the standard OpenProject API
findings.detail: Selecting api_v3 grants access to the standard OpenProject API. It is the default when no scope is checked. It is broader than read-only work package listing, so the app must limit its own calls to reads. Access to individual work packages still depends on the person's roles.

findings.title: Connected person needs access to the work packages
findings.detail: Work package visibility comes from the person's project roles. Users who are logged in and have view permission can see work packages. If the person cannot see work packages, the list call returns MissingPermission. Verify representative access before testing.
findings.appliesWhen: Connected person's existing account access is required for the list results.

findings.title: Access token expires after two hours by default
findings.detail: The bearer token expires after two hours by default and returns an error when used after expiry. A refresh token is issued and the app must request a new token. This is a token lifetime, not an approval wait.
findings.appliesWhen: Long-running reads or repeated paginated requests.

steps.title: Register OAuth application on the customer instance
steps.detail: Customer instance administrator opens Administration > Authentication > OAuth applications on the target OpenProject instance, clicks the green + OAuth application button, enters a name, sets the redirect URL to the developer's callback URL, selects the api_v3 scope, leaves Confidential checked for a server-side app, and clicks Create. Note the Client ID and Client secret. Only an administrator can create OAuth apps. The client secret is typically stored server-side.
steps.doneWhen: The OAuth application appears in the list with a Client ID and Client secret recorded in a secure store, and the redirect URL matches the developer callback.

steps.title: Obtain authorization code through the consent redirect
steps.detail: Open the authorization URL in a browser, signed in as the connected person. The person approves access, and OpenProject redirects to the registered redirect URL with a code query parameter. Confirm the callback receives the code and that the state/redirect matches. Do not treat this as completed until the callback contains the code.
steps.doneWhen: The redirect URL receives a code parameter after the connected person approves consent.

steps.title: Read first page of work packages (titles from subject)
steps.detail: Calls GET <INSTANCE_BASE_URL>/api/v3/work_packages with offset=1 and pageSize (e.g., 25) and filters=[] as documented query parameters, using the developer-owned OAuth bearer token for the customer's instance. Reads subject from each element in _embedded.elements, and reads total and count metadata from the collection. Only GET is used; no write or delete requests are made. Scope api_v3 is broader than read-only listing, so the app must limit its own calls to GET reads. Work package visibility still depends on the connected person's roles.
steps.doneWhen: Response is 200 JSON with _embedded.elements, each item containing subject, plus total and count metadata. Boundary check: with a safe nonmutating check, confirm the api_v3 grant matches documented read-only access; if an undocumented denied read occurs, inspect the grant and request log to confirm only requested GETs ran, with no prohibited modifications or deletions.
